question: ap1

parallel.problem: Do temporary historical events, such as colonial rule or wartime mobilization, persist through specific institutions so that they shape present-day outcomes long after the cause is gone?
parallel.how_studied: Scholars use spatial regression-discontinuity designs at historical borders, instrumental variables, and persistence regressions linking past exposure to present outcomes. They then do mediation analysis to test which carrier explains the persistence: formal institutions, cultural norms, or elite networks. Placebo tests on boundaries that had no institutional consequence, and cases where the institution was later abolished, help separate a real memory carrier from correlated geography.

prompt:
Here is a problem from another field that shares the underlying structure of the research question below, with notes on how that field investigates it.

<parallel>
Field: Political science (historical institutionalism)
Problem: Do temporary historical events, such as colonial rule or wartime mobilization, persist through specific institutions so that they shape present-day outcomes long after the cause is gone?
How it is studied: Scholars use spatial regression-discontinuity designs at historical borders, instrumental variables, and persistence regressions linking past exposure to present outcomes. They then do mediation analysis to test which carrier explains the persistence: formal institutions, cultural norms, or elite networks. Placebo tests on boundaries that had no institutional consequence, and cases where the institution was later abolished, help separate a real memory carrier from correlated geography.
</parallel>

Each of your ideas must transfer a specific method, measurement logic, or principle from how that field studies its problem, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the research question.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Persistence regression with lineage tracing and formal mediation
ideas.description: Expose cells to a transient stimulus, withdraw it, and track barcoded clones over many divisions with longitudinal scATAC/scRNA, regressing later response amplitude on past exposure dose. Then run mediation analysis to ask how much of the persistence coefficient is carried by retained AP-1 motif accessibility/FOS-JUN occupancy versus competing carriers such as DNA methylation, H3K4me1, BAF retention, or residual protein.

ideas.title: Abolish the institution: degron removal during the memory window
ideas.description: Apply an auxin/dTAG degron to FOS/JUN family members only after stimulus withdrawal and before restimulation, mimicking the political-science test of whether persistence survives abolition of the carrier. If AP-1 maintains memory, degradation confined to the latent period should erase enhanced recall despite an intact exposure history.

ideas.title: Placebo loci: matched AP-1 motifs that were never occupied
ideas.description: CRISPR-mutate AP-1 motifs that gained stable accessibility after the transient stimulus (the treated border) alongside sequence- and expression-matched motifs that were never occupied (the placebo border with no institutional consequence). Memory should be lost only for the first set, excluding generic AP-1 dependence or motif-adjacent genomic context.

ideas.title: Allele-level natural experiment in F1 hybrid cells
ideas.description: In F1 hybrid cells, use heterozygous SNPs that disrupt AP-1 motifs as a within-nucleus discontinuity: both alleles share an identical trans environment and exposure history, so allele-specific differences in retained priming and recall isolate cis AP-1 motif function. Motif-neutral heterozygous sites serve as the placebo comparison.

ideas.title: Dose-threshold discontinuity plus an orthogonal instrument
ideas.description: Finely titrate stimulus to locate the sharp threshold where AP-1 enhancer priming switches on, then compare cells just below versus just above the cutoff (sorted on a live AP-1 reporter) for long-term recall. Complement with instrumental-variable logic by inducing FOS/JUN optogenetically without the original stimulus, shifting AP-1 activity through a route that bypasses other stimulus-induced changes.
